update.title: Built an editable desktop HUD for Wayland
update.summary: Placed images, looping video, and live Graph Library widgets on a transparent desktop surface with in-place editing, reusable layouts, and runtime control.

preview.description: Images, live charts, gauges, and a looping fire effect composed across the desktop.

blocks.body:
## Assemble the desktop from elements

I built Desktop HUD as a transparent GTK4 layer-shell surface that places images, looping video, and live Graph Library widgets directly on the Wayland desktop. Each element shares identity, position, size, opacity, and visibility fields while its renderer handles type-specific behavior.

Outside edit mode, the overlay clears its input region, keeping the desktop click-through. Image and video playback remain inside their own elements while the HUD coordinates composition, lifecycle, and placement.

blocks.description: Two different looping fire versions: an opaque treatment and an alpha-transparent version that keeps the desktop visible through the flames.

blocks.body:
## Bring live data into the overlay

Graph Library supplies gauges and line charts as embeddable GTK widgets. Desktop HUD selects a renderer and provider, schedules refreshes, and places the result beside image and video elements without absorbing Graph Library’s data history or drawing logic.

By changing only the provider and renderer configuration, the same element model hosts command-backed gauges, rolling line charts, and static demonstration data.

blocks.description: Live system-load and CPU-temperature line charts rendered through Graph Library.
Compact CPU and memory gauges using the same graph element contract.

blocks.body:
## Edit the layout in place

Edit mode turns the rendered overlay itself into the design surface. Selecting an element reveals an outline and corner handles; dragging moves it, the handles resize it, and snapping aligns it with screen or neighboring element edges.

Each interaction updates the active element and visible widget together. Leaving edit mode removes the selection chrome and restores click-through behavior.

blocks.description: Edit mode exposes the selected element’s outline and resize handles directly on the rendered overlay.

blocks.body:
## Control the same model at runtime

A local HTTP API exposes explicit operations to list, add, update, and remove elements; reload configuration; toggle edit mode; check health; and manage profiles. It dispatches GTK mutations onto the application thread with a bounded wait, giving launchers and automation structured operations instead of arbitrary code execution.

Profile operations save, restore, switch, and combine named arrangements through the same runtime surface.

flowchart LR
  Profiles[Layout profiles] --> Model[Live element model]
  API[Local HTTP API] --> Model
  Editor[Drag resize snap] --> Model
  Model --> Image[Image elements]
  Model --> Video[Looping video]
  Model --> Graph[Graph Library widgets]
  Image --> Surface[GTK4 layer-shell surface]
  Video --> Surface
  Graph --> Surface
blocks.description: Profiles, runtime commands, and direct manipulation converge on the element model rendered on the layer-shell surface.
